subject: Cryptonio SIG follow-up: encryption key lifecycle & evidence packet request
thread_body:
--- Message 1 (original request) ---
From: Elena Varga <security@cryptonio.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@cryptonio.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG - encryption & key management clarifications (Cryptonio RFP)

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. As part of our SIG review and RFP, we need more detail on Redwood's encryption key lifecycle and proof artifacts for three specific asks:

1) KMS & key rotation: frequency, process owners, and sample rotation logs for a customer-managed key scenario.
2) HSM usage / key wrapping: evidence that keys used for production primitives are backed by an HSM or equivalent provider — any attestation or vendor support docs.
3) In-transit encryption: capture of TLS termination points across hosted/dedicated/private modes and where ephemeral keys are used.

Can you provide a concise control mapping (SIG/CCM control IDs) and a small evidence packet we can hand to our security operations team? Ideally by COB Tue (20 Apr).

Thanks,
Elena Varga
Head of Security Engineering
Cryptonio Payments

--- Message 2 (forward + triage) ---
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG - encryption & key management clarifications (Cryptonio RFP)

Folks — forwarding Cryptonio's asks. They want SIG mapping + an evidence packet by COB Tue. I think the ask is primarily about our KMS model (hosted keys vs customer-managed), rotation artifacts, and HSM proof. Marissa, can you lead the SIG mapping and include the SOC2 bridge note? Ben, can you pull rotation logs and a short explanation of key wrapping/HSM and where to find vendor attestations.

Summary of requested deliverables:
- SIG control mapping (reference IDs) -> where Redwood satisfies each item
- Redacted rotation log sample & description of rotation cadence and owner
- HSM/vendor attestation links and brief note on how we use key wrapping for private deploys
- TLS termination diagram highlighting public vs private termination points

I can join the call with Elena on Mon if helpful.

— Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

--- Message 3 (technical response) ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Varga <security@cryptonio.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG - encryption & key management clarifications (Cryptonio RFP)

Sergio / Marissa / Elena —

Below is a concise technical summary and pointers to artifacts we can include in the packet. I attach the rotation policy (redwood_kms_key_rotation_policy.pdf) and an architecture sketch (encryption-architecture-diagram.png).

1) KMS & key rotation
- Model: Redwood supports three models: hosted-managed keys (Redwood KMS), customer-managed KMS (BYOK via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault), and HSM-backed key wrapping for Private deployments.
- Rotation cadence: customer-managed keys follow customer's KMS policy; Redwood-managed master keys rotate on a 90-day cycle by default (configurable).
- Process owners: Key rotation is initiated by the CryptoOps team and tracked in Jira (ticket prefix CRYPTO-). Rotation is automated via our orchestration pipeline; manual approvals are logged.
- Artifact example: redacted rotation log sample (format: timestamp, key-id, action, operator-id, ticket-id). We will redact user IDs before sharing.

2) HSM / key wrapping
- For on-prem/private deployments, we support key wrapping where customer root keys are stored in their HSM; Redwood holds only wrapped DEKs (data encryption keys).
- Vendor attestations: We rely on FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules via the cloud KMS provider (links included in the evidence bundle). For self-hosted HSMs, customers provide attestation; we accept vendor-signed module certs.

3) In-transit encryption & TLS termination
- Hosted API: TLS is terminated at our load balancer in the region; mutual TLS is supported for dedicated/private tenants.
- Dedicated/Private: TLS termination can be customer-managed (VPC termination) or Redwood-managed within the customer's private VPC depending on contract.
- Where ephemeral keys are used: inter-node RPCs use short-lived mTLS certificates issued by our internal CA (rotated daily).

Attach list (will include in packet):
- redwood_kms_key_rotation_policy.pdf (internal policy, redaction-ready)
- encryption-architecture-diagram.png (annotated: termination points and mTLS path)
- soc2-bridge-statement.docx (explanation of how SOC 2 controls map to SIG/CCM)

Next steps: Marissa, can you assemble the SIG mapping table and the short SOC2 bridge stmt; Sergio, can you coordinate delivery and confirm whether Cryptonio prefers a signed attestation or simply the vendor links + redacted logs.

— Ben
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

--- Message 4 (compliance mapping) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Varga <security@cryptonio.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG - encryption & key management clarifications (Cryptonio RFP)

Elena / team —

I've drafted the SIG-to-Redwood control mapping and included a one-page SOC 2 bridge statement that highlights control owners and evidence locations. Highlights below:

- SIG CC6 (Cryptographic Controls) -> Covered by KMS key rotation policy + rotation logs + HSM key wrapping design (evidence files: redwood_kms_key_rotation_policy.pdf, encryption-architecture-diagram.png).
- SIG IPY (Infrastructure protection) -> mTLS and ephemeral certificate rotation logs (we can provide CSR/rotation meta, redacted).
- SIG CIV (Change & config) -> Jira CRYPTO workflow for rotation and approval traces (we can provide ticket IDs and redacted audit trails).

Packaging plan:
- Packet A (customer-ready): SOC2 bridge (soc2-bridge-statement.docx), architecture diagram, sanitized rotation log extract.
- Packet B (legal/attestation): vendor FIPS cert links and compliance declarations (we will not share raw HSM certs unless requested and an NDA is in place).

Requested clarification for delivery: do you want Packet A delivered now and Packet B after we have a signed NDA? I recommend Packet A to unblock your SecOps review.

I will assemble the mapping table as CSV and include inline references to our SOC2 control IDs and the specific artifact filenames. Sharing target: Tue EOD US/PST.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance & Assurance
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--- Message 5 (external ack + question) ---
From: Elena Varga <security@cryptonio.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cryptonio SIG follow-up: encryption key lifecycle & evidence packet request

Thanks, team — that all looks good. We prefer Packet A now to proceed with our SecOps review; Packet B is fine behind an NDA. Two quick clarifying Qs:

1) For redacted rotation logs: can you include the ticket-id and time-range but remove operator email/usernames? That will let us tie activity to change events during our sampling.
2) For the SOC2 bridge: can you explicitly call out the SOC2 CC6 sub-control IDs and whether the evidence provided is "control evidence" or "design only" (we mark in our intake).

If you can get Packet A into a shared Drive link by tomorrow morning we can continue the intake and aim to have an initial risk memo back by next week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Elena
Head of Security Engineering, Cryptonio Payments
security@cryptonio.com

[Attachments referenced: redwood_kms_key_rotation_policy.pdf (PDF, 178KB); encryption-architecture-diagram.png (PNG, 240KB); soc2-bridge-statement.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]
